en.title: Advancing Clean Water and Resilient Cities, PT Vale and Indonesia’s Ministry of Environment Remove Over 56 Tons of Waste from Cipinang River
en.subtitle: PT Vale Indonesia Tbk, part of the Mining Industry Indonesia (MIND ID) Group, partnered with the Ministry of Environment and Forestry (KLHK) to launch the 2025 Cipinang River Clean-Up Movement. This national initiative aims to improve water quality, raise public awareness, and strengthen community engagement across East Jakarta and Depok.
en.body:
Jakarta, October 21, 2025 — Rivers are more than just waterways—they are vital ecosystems and lifelines for urban communities. In a strong show of collaboration and environmental stewardship, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk, part of the Mining Industry Indonesia (MIND ID) Group, partnered with the Ministry of Environment and Forestry (KLHK) to launch the 2025 Cipinang River Clean-Up Movement. This national initiative aims to improve water quality, raise public awareness, and strengthen community engagement across East Jakarta and Depok.

Led by Minister Hanif Faisol Nurofiq, the movement has mobilized hundreds of volunteers and stakeholders. By mid-October, 225 community members had helped remove over 56 tons of waste from the river and its banks. The initiative also installed 19 trash booms and CCTV units at key locations to intercept and monitor waste flow. Data from Jakarta’s Environmental Agency revealed that in September alone, 302 tons of waste were recorded in the river—highlighting the urgency of collective action.

“Rivers are the lifeblood of our cities. The formation of the Cipinang River Community marks the beginning of a long-term commitment to clean water, flood prevention, and a new urban culture,” said Minister Hanif.

KLHK emphasized that effective river management relies not only on technology but also on public discipline and active participation. Dr. Rasio “Roy” Ridho Sani, Deputy for Pollution and Environmental Damage Control, stressed the importance of integrity and enforcement. “Environmental discipline must start with individuals and institutions. This movement shows that collaboration between government, communities, and businesses can drive real change,” he said.

For PT Vale, this initiative reflects more than corporate responsibility—it embodies the company’s sustainability philosophy, which recognizes water as a shared resource essential to life. As a nickel mining company powered entirely by renewable hydroelectric energy in South Sulawesi, PT Vale understands that clean water is fundamental to sustainable industry, healthy communities, and thriving ecosystems. 

Through this collaboration, PT Vale is extending its best practices in water management and conservation from its operational areas to urban environments, where waste and pollution require cross-sector solutions.

“Water sustains not only our operations but also our communities. This movement aligns with Vale’s belief that every drop of water must be protected and returned cleaner. We’re proud to support KLHK’s efforts to build a culture of river stewardship,” said Budiawansyah, Director & Chief of Sustainability and Corporate Affairs Officer, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk.

Activities continue this week in Depok and East Jakarta, including river clean-ups, community training, and the launch of the Peduli Lingkungan app—designed to enhance community-based environmental monitoring. The initiative is expected to serve as a scalable model for sustainable public–private–community partnerships across Indonesia.

On October 19, Minister Hanif convened an evaluation meeting in Depok with local government officials, parliament representatives, and river community leaders. The forum reaffirmed the importance of sustaining the movement and building community capacity to protect the ecological function of the Cipinang River. PT Vale reiterated its commitment to supporting environmental restoration and water literacy through collaborative, science-based, and behavior-driven approaches.

The Cipinang River Movement has become a symbol of hope and collaboration—demonstrating that protecting rivers means protecting life. Every sack of waste removed, every volunteer engaged, and every drop of clean water restored reflects the power of collective action.

Pria Utama, Corporate Secretary of MIND ID, echoed this sentiment: “Rivers are not just water flows—they are sources of life and energy that support our national mining operations. Downstreaming is not only about economic value; it’s about ensuring industrial progress goes hand-in-hand with environmental preservation. With a spirit of collaboration, we will continue to protect rivers as vital energy for building the future of civilization.”

id.title: Angkat Lebih dari 56 Ton Sampah dari Sungai Cipinang, PT Vale Bersama KLHK Wujudkan Kolaborasi Nyata Menuju Air Bersih dan Kota Berdaya
id.subtitle: PT Vale Indonesia Tbk bagian dari Grup Mining Industry (MIND ID) bersama Kementerian Lingkungan Hidup (KLH) bergandengan tangan dalam Gerakan Bersih Sungai Cipinang 2025, sebuah inisiatif nasional untuk memulihkan kualitas air, menumbuhkan kesadaran masyarakat, dan memperkuat jejaring komunitas sungai di wilayah Jakarta Timur dan Depok.
id.body:
Jakarta, 21 Oktober 2025 — Sungai bukan sekadar aliran air; ia adalah urat nadi kehidupan kota dan penentu masa depan lingkungan yang kita wariskan. Dengan semangat kolaborasi dan keberlanjutan, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk bagian dari Grup Mining Industry (MIND ID) bersama Kementerian Lingkungan Hidup (KLH) bergandengan tangan dalam Gerakan Bersih Sungai Cipinang 2025, sebuah inisiatif nasional untuk memulihkan kualitas air, menumbuhkan kesadaran masyarakat, dan memperkuat jejaring komunitas sungai di wilayah Jakarta Timur dan Depok.

Gerakan yang berada di bawah arahan Menteri Lingkungan Hidup/Kepala Badan Pengendalian Lingkungan Hidup, Hanif Faisol Nurofiq, ini telah menggerakkan energi kolektif dari berbagai lapisan masyarakat. Hingga pertengahan Oktober, sebanyak 225 relawan komunitas Sungai Cipinang telah terlibat dalam kegiatan gotong royong di empat segmen utama, mengangkat lebih dari 56 ton sampah dari badan dan bantaran sungai, serta mendukung pemasangan 19 unit trashboom dan CCTV di titik strategis untuk menahan serta memantau aliran sampah. Catatan Dinas Lingkungan Hidup DKI Jakarta bahkan menunjukkan bahwa sepanjang September 2025, beban sampah yang teridentifikasi di aliran Sungai Cipinang telah mencapai 302 ton, mempertegas urgensi aksi bersama ini. “Sungai adalah urat nadi kota yang harus dijaga bersama. Pengukuhan Komunitas Sungai Cipinang bukan akhir, tetapi awal dari gerakan panjang menjaga air bersih, mengurangi risiko banjir, dan membangun budaya baru bagi kota-kota kita,”
ujar Hanif.

Kementerian menegaskan bahwa keberhasilan pengelolaan sungai tidak hanya bergantung pada teknologi, tetapi juga pada kedisiplinan dan partisipasi masyarakat. Hal itu disampaikan pula oleh Dr. Rasio “Roy” Ridho Sani, Deputi Bidang Pengendalian Pencemaran dan Kerusakan Lingkungan, yang menekankan pentingnya integritas dan penegakan hukum dalam menjaga kualitas air. “Kita tidak bisa bicara pengelolaan tanpa penegakan hukum. Disiplin lingkungan harus dimulai dari individu hingga institusi. Gerakan ini membuktikan bahwa sinergi pemerintah, masyarakat, dan dunia usaha dapat menghasilkan dampak nyata,” ujar Roy.

Bagi PT Vale, partisipasi dalam gerakan ini bukan sekadar kegiatan tanggung jawab sosial, melainkan bagian dari filosofi keberlanjutan perusahaan yang menempatkan air sebagai sumber kehidupan yang harus dijaga bersama. Sebagai perusahaan tambang nikel yang mengandalkan energi 100% terbarukan dari pembangkit listrik tenaga air (PLTA) di Sulawesi Selatan, PT Vale memahami bahwa air bersih adalah fondasi dari keberlanjutan industri, masyarakat, dan lingkungan. Melalui kolaborasi ini, Vale berupaya memperluas praktik terbaik dalam pengelolaan air dan konservasi lingkungan dari kawasan operasi ke ruang perkotaan — di mana tantangan sampah dan polusi air membutuhkan keterlibatan aktif lintas sektor. “Air adalah sumber kehidupan, bukan hanya bagi tambang, tetapi juga bagi masyarakat. Gerakan ini sejalan dengan filosofi Vale bahwa setiap tetes air harus dijaga dan dikembalikan lebih bersih. Kami bangga menjadi bagian dari inisiatif KLHK dalam memperkuat budaya peduli sungai,” tutur Budiawansyah, Director & Chief of Sustainability and Corporate Affairs Officer (CSCAO), PT Vale Indonesia Tbk.

Pekan ini, kegiatan akan terus berlanjut di wilayah Depok dan Jakarta Timur dengan agenda bersih sungai, pembekalan komunitas, dan sosialisasi aplikasi Peduli Lingkungan yang dikembangkan untuk memperkuat sistem pemantauan berbasis masyarakat. Inisiatif ini diharapkan menjadi model kolaborasi lintas pemangku kepentingan (public–private–community partnership) yang berkelanjutan dan dapat direplikasi di daerah lain di Indonesia.

Sebagai tindak lanjut dari rangkaian kegiatan ini, pada 19 Oktober 2025 Menteri Lingkungan Hidup Hanif Faisol Nurofiq memimpin langsung rapat evaluasi di Depok bersama para pemangku kepentingan, termasuk perwakilan pemerintah daerah, DPRD, dan komunitas sungai. Pertemuan tersebut menegaskan kembali pentingnya kesinambungan gerakan dan peningkatan kapasitas komunitas dalam menjaga kebersihan dan fungsi ekologis Sungai Cipinang. Dalam forum itu, PT Vale turut menyampaikan komitmennya untuk terus mendukung program pemulihan lingkungan dan penguatan literasi air melalui pendekatan kolaboratif, berbasis sains, dan berorientasi pada perubahan perilaku.

Gerakan Sungai Cipinang kini menjadi simbol kolaborasi dan harapan — bahwa menjaga sungai berarti menjaga kehidupan. Dari setiap karung sampah yang diangkat, setiap relawan yang terlibat, dan setiap tetes air yang kembali mengalir jernih, kita belajar bahwa perubahan besar dimulai dari langkah-langkah kecil yang dilakukan bersama.

Corporate Secretary MIND ID, Pria Utama, menegaskan, sungai bukan sekadar tentang aliran air, tetapi sumber kehidupan sekaligus energi yang menopang berbagai aktivitas bagi industri pertambangan nasional Grup MIND ID.

Oleh karena, perseroan bersama seluruh Anggota terus berupaya memastikan sungai dapat terus hidup dan menghidupi serta terus mampu menjadi penopang bagi keberlanjutan operasional sekaligus keseimbangan alam di masa depan.

“Hilirisasi yang Grup MIND ID jalankan bukan hanya soal menciptakan nilai tambah ekonomi, tetapi memastikan kemajuan industri berjalan berdampingan kelestarian dengan alam. Dengan semangat kolaborasi, kami akan terus menjaga sungai sehingga mampu menjadi energi bagi pembangunan peradaban masa depan," katanya.

en.title: From Loeha Raya: PT Vale Champions Literacy for Indonesia’s Future Leaders Through Book Donations
en.subtitle: In a meaningful step toward cultivating a generation of well-informed, globally competitive youth—those poised to enter the prime of their professional lives as Indonesia celebrates its centennial of independence in 2045—PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PT Vale), a subsidiary of Mining Industry Indonesia (MIND ID), has reaffirmed its commitment to education by donating books to children in Loeha Raya, located in the Tanamalia Block.
en.body:
Sorowako, October 20, 2025 – In a meaningful step toward cultivating a generation of well-informed, globally competitive youth—those poised to enter the prime of their professional lives as Indonesia celebrates its centennial of independence in 2045—PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PT Vale), a subsidiary of Mining Industry Indonesia (MIND ID), has reaffirmed its commitment to education by donating books to children in Loeha Raya, located in the Tanamalia Block.

The donation was formally handed over to the management of the Jendela Dunia (Window to the World) Library in Tokalimbo Village on Monday, October 20, 2025, during a ceremony held at PT Vale’s GFS office in Sorowako, East Luwu, South Sulawesi.

The donation package included hundreds of children’s storybooks, encyclopedias, science comics, writing supplies, and study desks. This initiative aligns with Indonesia’s national vision to foster educational advancement and intellectual development across all regions, ensuring that every child has access to quality learning resources.

This effort reflects PT Vale’s deep-rooted commitment to enhancing literacy among children in Loeha Raya. Recognizing books as gateways to knowledge and imagination, the company aims to bridge educational gaps caused by geographic isolation and limited infrastructure. In remote areas where transportation can be a barrier, such initiatives become vital in ensuring that children are not left behind in their pursuit of learning.

Mercy Balebu, Senior Project Manager of Tanamalia PT Vale, emphasized that the donation was made possible through the voluntary contributions of PT Vale employees and contractors. She highlighted the company’s broader mission to uplift communities through education.

“Our mission is to improve the quality of life in every area where we operate,” Mercy stated. “Through this book donation, we hope to inspire children to dream big and pursue their aspirations. We believe that access to books can ignite curiosity and open doors to endless possibilities.”

She further noted that this marks the first book donation in the Tanamalia area, with plans to expand the program to other villages based on community assessments and identified needs.

“The digital age presents new challenges for educators,” Mercy added. “Children are increasingly drawn to mobile devices rather than books. It’s crucial that we work together to address this shift. We must reintroduce children to the joy of reading—whether through physical books or digital formats.”

Hasni Nusia Sari, a staff member at the Jendela Dunia Library, expressed heartfelt appreciation for PT Vale’s support. She recounted her surprise and emotion upon learning about the donation.

“I was at a loss as to where else to turn for help in acquiring books that could attract children to the library,” Hasni shared. “I’m truly grateful for the company’s support.”

She explained that while the village allocates a modest annual budget for book purchases, the limited funds have made it difficult to obtain engaging materials that spark children’s interest in reading.

“Thank you so much, PT Vale,” Hasni said with gratitude. “I’m thrilled that the company genuinely cares about children’s literacy in our village. With these books—especially the illustrated storybooks—I’m confident more children will be drawn to the library.”

Hasni also shared that the library has become a regular stop for elementary school children after classes. Initially, the children showed little interest, but over time, creative activities were introduced to cultivate their enthusiasm for reading.

As a community leader in Tokalimbo Village, Hasni believes in proactive change. “It’s better to light a candle than curse the darkness,” she said. Amid the challenges posed by digital distractions, she hopes the spirit of literacy will flourish not only in her village but across all of Loeha Raya, inspiring the creation of vibrant learning spaces in every community.

 
Sustained Commitment to Educational Development
PT Vale’s dedication to education extends far beyond book and stationery donations. The company has long been actively involved in ensuring that formal education within its operational areas meets national standards and supports the holistic development of students.

Since 2023, PT Vale has rolled out a series of impactful programs, including vocational training, university entrance preparation courses, and workshops on the Merdeka Curriculum—Indonesia’s progressive education framework. These initiatives aim to strengthen the competencies of educators from kindergarten through junior high school in Loeha Raya, equipping them to better nurture the next generation.

In addition to formal education, PT Vale also supports environmental education. The company regularly hosts educational visits from local institutions such as the Bantilang Village English Course and SD 279 Rante Angin, offering students hands-on learning experiences in sustainable practices and environmental stewardship.

Endra Kusuma, Director of External Relations at PT Vale, underscored the company’s focus on sustainability and its integral connection to education.
“Sustainability is at the heart of our operations,” Endra stated. “Education plays a critical role in shaping the quality of local talent—individuals who may one day become part of our workforce. We are committed to empowering local communities by investing in their future, starting with education.”

PT Vale remains steadfast in its pledge to contribute positively to both the communities and the environment surrounding its operational areas. Through initiatives like these, the company continues to build a legacy of impact—one book, one child, and one village at a time.

id.title: Dari Loeha Raya, PT Vale Tingkatkan Minat Baca Generasi Emas Lewat Donasi Buku
id.subtitle: Wujudkan generasi emas yang memiliki literasi luas, berdaya saing dan berdaya guna, anak usaha Mining Industry (MIND ID), PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PT Vale) menunjukkan komitmennya melalui penyerahan donasi buku untuk anak-anak Loeha Raya, Blok Tanamalia. Generasi emas adalah generasi muda yang akan memasuki usia produktif saat Indonesia merayakan 100 tahun kemerdekaannya pada 2045.
id.body:
Sorowako, 20 Oktober 2025 - Wujudkan generasi emas yang memiliki literasi luas, berdaya saing dan berdaya guna, anak usaha Mining Industry (MIND ID), PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PT Vale) menunjukkan komitmennya melalui penyerahan donasi buku untuk anak-anak Loeha Raya, Blok Tanamalia. Generasi emas adalah generasi muda yang akan memasuki usia produktif saat Indonesia merayakan 100 tahun kemerdekaannya pada 2045.

Penyerahan donasi ke pengelola Perpustakaan Jendela Dunia Desa Tokalimbo dilakukan pada Senin (20/10/2025) di kantor GFS, Sorowako, Luwu Timur, Sulawesi Selatan.

Donasi diberikan dalam bentuk berupa ratusan buku cerita anak, ensiklopedia, komik sains serta alat tulis dan meja belajar.  Upaya tersebut sejalan dengan amanat negara untuk mencerdaskan segala bangsa sehingga dunia pendidikan terus maju. 

Kegiatan dilakukan sebagai bentuk kepedulian perusahaan dalam meningkatkan literasi anak di Loeha Raya. Buku sebagai jendela dunia perlu disalurkan dan dinikmati oleh siapa saja. Jangan sampai akses transportasi menjadi halangan seorang anak untuk memperoleh pengetahuan.

Senior Project Manager Tanamalia PT Vale, Mercy Balebu mengatakan, donasi yang diberikan adalah hasil sumbangan sukarela para karyawan dan kontraktor. Perseroan mendukung agar anak-anak memiliki pengetahuan dengan membaca buku.

“Perusahaan memiliki misi untuk meningkatkan kualitas hidup di setiap wilayah operasionalnya. Melalui donasi buku ini, terselip harapan agar anak-anak bisa berani bermimpi dan menggapi cita-citanya,” katanya.

Tidak hanya itu, Mercy juga menyampaikan pemberian buku ini merupakan yang pertama di wilayah Tanamalia. Program diharapkan dapat berkelanjutan ke beberapa area desa-desa lainnya menyesuaikan dengan kebutuhan masyarakat berdasarkan asesmen di lapangan. 

“Dunia digital saat ini memberi tantangan kepada para pengajar. Anak-anak lebih senang bermain handphone dibanding membaca. Mari bekerja sama memecahkan tantangan ini. Anak perlu didekatkan pada dunia buku baik dalam bentuk fisik ataupun elektronik,” harap Mercy.

Staf Pengelola Perpustakaan Jendela Dunia Hasni Nusia Sari menyampaikan rasa haru dan simpati atas kepedulian PT Vale. Bahkan, dia mengaku kaget sekaligus terharu saat mendapat informasi ada donasi buku dan alat tulis tersebut.

"Saya sudah pusing harus meminta bantuan buku ke mana lagi agar anak-anak bisa tertarik ke perpustakaan, syukurlah ada bantuan dan kepedulian dari perusahaan," ungkapnya.

Hasni bercerita setiap tahunnya desa memiliki anggaran pembelian buku. Namun, dengan anggaran terbatas buku yang dimiliki juga belum sepenuhnya menarik minat anak untuk singgah belajar di perpustakaan. 

“Terima kasih banyak PT Vale. Saya senang perusahaan betul-betul memperhatikan literasi anak-anak di desa. Melalui buku-buku ini saya yakin anak-anak akan tertarik ke perpustakaan, apalagi banyak buku cerita bergambar yang diberikan,” kata Hasni penuh syukur. 

Ia berbagi selama ini perpustakaannya menjadi tempat singgah anak usia SD saat pulang sekolah. Awal mulanya anak-anak belum tertarik, perlahan kegiatan kreavitas diadakan untuk menumbuhkan minat ke perpustakaan. 

Pengurus Desa Tokalimbo ini percaya lebih baik menyalakan lilin daripada mengutuk kegelapan. Di tengah tantangan digital, Ia berharap semangat literasi tidak hanya tumbuh di desanya. Tetapi setiap desa di Loeha Raya turut menciptakan sarana belajar yang baik. 

Konsisten Pengembangan di Dunia Pendidikan

Tidak hanya melakukan pemberian donasi buku dan alat tulis, kepedulian PT Vale di dunia pendidikan sudah dimulai sejak lama. Perseroan ikut memastikan pendidikan yang dilakukan melalui bangku sekolah berjalan sesuai dengan standar. 

Sejak tahun 2023, PT Vale mulai melakukan berbagai program seperti Pelatihan Vokasional, Bimbingan Belajar Masuk Perguruan Tinggi serta Pelatihan Kurikulum Merdeka untuk memastikan guru TK hingga SMP di Loeha Raya memiliki kompetensi yang baik dalam mencerdaskan anak bangsa. 

Di sisi lain, perusahaan juga berkontribusi menjadi sarana belajar pengelolaan lingkungan yang baik. Hal ini dibuktikan dengan menerima kunjungan belajar dari Lembaga Kursus Bahasa Inggris Desa Bantilang dan SD 279 Rante Angin. 

Direktur Eksternal Relations Endra Kusuma menyatakan aspek keberlanjutan menjadi fokus utama PT Vale dalam beroperasi. Adapun dunia pendidikan merupakan aspek penting penentu kualitas talenta-talenta lokal yang akan berkarya di perusahaan. 

“Kami berkomitmen memberdayakan talenta lokal untuk menjadi SDM unggul. Sejak dini, kami turut memastikan kualitas anak bangsa dalam segi pendidikan,” tuturnya. 

Perusahaan memastikan kontribusi-kontribusi positif akan terus dilakukan untuk masyarakat juga lingkungan di sekitar wilayah operasionalnya.

en.title: Confronting a Silent Epidemic: PT Vale Indonesia Advances a Healthier, Cleaner, and Empowered Kolaka Through HIV-AIDS and Tuberculosis Awareness Campaign
en.subtitle: Through its Indonesia Growth Project (IGP) Pomalaa, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PT Vale) organized a community outreach program focused on the prevention of HIV-AIDS and Tuberculosis (TB), held in Kampung Bajo, Dawi-Dawi Village, Pomalaa District. This initiative is a key component of the Kolaka Sehat, Bersih, dan Berdaya (Healthy, Clean, and Empowered Kolaka) Program, a collaborative effort between PT Vale and the Kolaka Regional Government aimed at improving public health and community resilience in the region.
en.body:
Kolaka, October 16, 2025 — As part of its ongoing commitment to sustainable development, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk, a leading sustainable nickel producer, has launched a public health awareness initiative in Pomalaa, Southeast Sulawesi. Through its Indonesia Growth Project (IGP) Pomalaa, the company organized a community outreach program focused on the prevention of HIV-AIDS and Tuberculosis (TB), held in Kampung Bajo, Dawi-Dawi Village, Pomalaa District.

This initiative is a key component of the Kolaka Sehat, Bersih, dan Berdaya (Healthy, Clean, and Empowered Kolaka) Program, a collaborative effort between PT Vale and the Kolaka Regional Government aimed at improving public health and community resilience in the region.

Partnering with the Pomalaa Community Health Center (Puskesmas) and local authorities, the campaign seeks to raise awareness about the risks of infectious diseases in the rapidly developing industrial zone of Pomalaa. As the area experiences increased population mobility due to industrial growth, the need for proactive health education and disease prevention becomes more urgent.

HIV-AIDS and TB remain significant global health concerns. Indonesia ranks among the top 30 countries with the highest TB burden, reporting over one million cases annually, including approximately 24,000 cases among individuals living with HIV. Locally, Kolaka Regency is witnessing a similar upward trend.

According to the 2023 Kolaka Health Profile, 46 new HIV cases were recorded—an increase from 34 the previous year—with 56.5% occurring among individuals in their most productive years. Men accounted for 80.4% of these cases, and 67% of patients have begun antiretroviral therapy (ARV).

For TB, surveillance data revealed 305 confirmed cases out of 1,514 suspected individuals, with fluctuations influenced by social and environmental factors in the region.

These figures underscore the importance of heightened vigilance and community engagement in preventing the spread of infectious diseases, especially in areas experiencing rapid industrialization.

Dr. Alriani Hamzah, Head of the Pomalaa Community Health Center, emphasized the importance of cross-sector collaboration in tackling infectious diseases. “As industrial activity brings more people into the region, the risk of disease transmission increases. We deeply appreciate this partnership, which strengthens our efforts to prevent and manage these health challenges more effectively,” she said.

 
Pomalaa District Head, Rachmat Hidayat Gavoer, echoed the sentiment, stressing that HIV-AIDS prevention is a shared responsibility. “The influx of workers from outside the region raises the potential for HIV-AIDS transmission. We commend PT Vale for taking proactive steps through this awareness campaign. People should not fear seeking treatment—HIV is manageable with consistent care,” he affirmed.

From the company’s perspective, Achmad Siswandi Asdam, Project Engineer for PT Vale IGP Pomalaa, highlighted that community health initiatives are integral to the company’s Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework.

“The signing of our Memorandum of Understanding with the Kolaka Regional Government marks a pivotal moment in our collaboration with local authorities and communities. We are committed to ensuring that every aspect of our operations contributes positively to environmental sustainability and community well-being,” he stated.

He added, “Through health education, medical equipment donations, scholarships for specialist doctors, and certification programs for healthcare workers, we aim to ensure that Kolaka residents have access to quality, sustainable healthcare. These efforts will be extended to all community health centers in Pomalaa.”

The campaign also promotes early disease detection and routine health screenings, encouraging residents to take proactive steps in safeguarding their health.

“Early detection is key to protecting our communities,” Achmad emphasized. “We will continue these efforts as part of our long-term commitment to community empowerment in our operational areas.”

This initiative is part of PT Vale’s broader strategy to build community health resilience—an essential pillar of sustainable development. The collaboration aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3: Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages.

Under the Kolaka Sehat, Bersih, dan Berdaya Program, PT Vale will implement a series of targeted actions, including:

  • Health education campaigns across villages and schools to prevent HIV-AIDS and TB
  • Capacity-building for healthcare professionals through training and certification
  • Provision of medical equipment to Pomalaa Type D Regional Hospital
  • Scholarships for specialist doctors to strengthen local healthcare human resources
  • Development of community-based early detection systems in collaboration with local health centers

As Pomalaa continues to grow into a key industrial hub in Southeast Sulawesi, PT Vale recognizes that true progress must be accompanied by a healthy, informed, and empowered population.

“Through our unwavering commitment to health, environmental stewardship, and community empowerment, PT Vale is dedicated to driving meaningful and sustainable change. Together with local government and communities, we are working to build a healthier, cleaner, and more resilient Kolaka,” Achmad Siswandi Asdam concluded.

id.title: Melawan Wabah Tersembunyi: PT Vale Indonesia Wujudkan Kolaka Sehat, Bersih, dan Berdaya melalui Sosialisasi Pencegahan HIV-AIDS dan TB
id.subtitle: PT Vale Indonesia Tbk melalui proyek Indonesia Growth Project (IGP) Pomalaa kembali menunjukkan komitmennya terhadap pembangunan berkelanjutan dengan menyelenggarakan kegiatan Sosialisasi Pencegahan HIV-AIDS dan Tuberkulosis (TB) bagi masyarakat Pomalaa. Kegiatan yang digelar di Jalan Kerapu, Kampung Bajo, Kelurahan Dawi-Dawi, Kecamatan Pomalaa ini merupakan bagian dari implementasi Program Kolaka Sehat, Bersih, dan Berdaya yang diluncurkan bersama Pemerintah Daerah Kolaka.
id.body:
Kolaka, 16 Oktober 2025 — Perusahaan nickel berkelanjutan, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk melalui proyek Indonesia Growth Project (IGP) Pomalaa kembali menunjukkan komitmennya terhadap pembangunan berkelanjutan dengan menyelenggarakan kegiatan Sosialisasi Pencegahan HIV-AIDS dan Tuberkulosis (TB) bagi masyarakat Pomalaa. Kegiatan yang digelar di Jalan Kerapu, Kampung Bajo, Kelurahan Dawi-Dawi, Kecamatan Pomalaa ini merupakan bagian dari implementasi Program Kolaka Sehat, Bersih, dan Berdaya yang diluncurkan bersama Pemerintah Daerah Kolaka.

Melalui kolaborasi dengan Puskesmas Pomalaa dan pemerintah setempat, kegiatan ini bertujuan meningkatkan kesadaran masyarakat terhadap bahaya penyakit menular berisiko tinggi di tengah pesatnya pertumbuhan kawasan industri Pomalaa.

Penyakit HIV-AIDS dan TB masih menjadi tantangan kesehatan global. Indonesia termasuk dalam 30 negara dengan beban TB tertinggi di dunia, dengan lebih dari 1 juta kasus TB setiap tahunnya dan sekitar 24.000 kasus TB di antara penderita HIV. Di tingkat lokal, Kabupaten Kolaka turut menghadapi tren peningkatan kasus serupa.

Berdasarkan Profil Kesehatan Kabupaten Kolaka 2023, terdapat 46 kasus baru HIV—meningkat dari 34 kasus di tahun sebelumnya—dan sekitar 56,5% di antaranya terjadi pada kelompok usia produktif. Mayoritas penderita merupakan laki-laki (80,4%) dan 67% dari kasus telah mendapatkan pengobatan ARV.
Untuk kasus Tuberkulosis (TB), surveilans mencatat 305 pasien positif dari 1.514 orang terduga TB, dengan pola fluktuatif yang dipengaruhi kondisi sosial dan iklim di wilayah tersebut.

Data ini menunjukkan bahwa peningkatan mobilitas penduduk akibat pertumbuhan industri menuntut kewaspadaan lebih tinggi terhadap penyebaran penyakit menular di masyarakat.

Kepala Puskesmas Pomalaa, dr. Alriani Hamzah, menyampaikan pentingnya sinergi lintas pihak dalam menanggulangi penyakit menular. “Dengan meningkatnya jumlah penduduk akibat aktivitas industri, risiko penyebaran penyakit menular juga meningkat. Karena itu, kami sangat mengapresiasi kolaborasi ini untuk menanggulangi dan mencegah penyebaran penyakit secara lebih efektif,” ujarnya.

Sementara itu, Camat Pomalaa, Rachmat Hidayat Gavoer, menekankan bahwa pencegahan HIV-AIDS adalah tanggung jawab bersama. “Banyaknya tenaga kerja dari luar dapat meningkatkan risiko penyebaran HIV-AIDS. Kami mengapresiasi langkah PT Vale yang proaktif melaksanakan kegiatan sosialisasi ini. Jangan takut untuk berobat, karena HIV bisa dikendalikan dengan pengobatan rutin,” tegasnya.
 

 

Dari sisi perusahaan, Achmad Siswandi Asdam, Project Engineer PT Vale IGP Pomalaa, menegaskan bahwa program kesehatan masyarakat menjadi bagian penting dari pilar Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) perusahaan.

“Penandatanganan MoU dengan Pemda Kolaka menjadi tonggak penting kolaborasi antara PT Vale, pemerintah, dan masyarakat. Kami ingin memastikan setiap langkah operasional perusahaan memberi dampak positif bagi kelestarian lingkungan dan kesejahteraan masyarakat,” ujarnya.

“Melalui edukasi kesehatan, bantuan alat medis, beasiswa dokter spesialis, dan sertifikasi tenaga kesehatan, kami ingin memastikan masyarakat Kolaka memiliki akses kesehatan yang layak dan berkelanjutan. Upaya ini akan terus bergulir ke seluruh Puskesmas di Pomalaa,” tambahnya.

Melalui kegiatan ini, PT Vale juga berkolaborasi dalam promosi kesehatan dan deteksi dini, mendorong masyarakat melakukan pemeriksaan rutin guna mencegah penyebaran penyakit sejak dini.

“Melalui deteksi dini, kita berharap masyarakat dapat terlindungi sejak awal. Upaya-upaya seperti ini akan terus kami lakukan secara berkelanjutan di wilayah pemberdayaan perusahaan,” tegas Achmad.

Program ini merupakan bagian dari strategi jangka panjang PT Vale untuk membangun ketahanan kesehatan komunitas sebagai elemen penting dari pembangunan berkelanjutan. Kolaborasi ini sejalan dengan Tujuan Pembangunan Berkelanjutan (SDGs) poin ke-3, yakni “Menjamin Kehidupan yang Sehat dan Meningkatkan Kesejahteraan untuk Semua Usia.”

Sebagai langkah nyata, PT Vale melalui Program Kolaka Sehat, Bersih, dan Berdaya akan melaksanakan:
•    Edukasi lintas desa dan sekolah untuk pencegahan HIV-AIDS dan TB;
•    Peningkatan kapasitas tenaga medis melalui pelatihan dan sertifikasi;
•    Bantuan alat kesehatan bagi RSUD Tipe D Pomalaa;
•    Beasiswa dokter spesialis untuk memperkuat sumber daya manusia kesehatan lokal;
•    Pembangunan sistem deteksi dini berbasis komunitas bersama Puskesmas.

Pertumbuhan kawasan industri Pomalaa menjadikan Kolaka sebagai salah satu motor ekonomi baru di Sulawesi Tenggara. Namun, PT Vale percaya bahwa kemajuan sejati hanya dapat dicapai jika disertai dengan masyarakat yang sehat, sadar, dan berdaya.

“Melalui komitmen terhadap kesehatan, kelestarian lingkungan, dan pemberdayaan masyarakat, PT Vale hadir untuk mendorong perubahan yang nyata dan berkelanjutan. Bersama pemerintah dan masyarakat, kami ingin mewujudkan Kolaka yang lebih sehat, bersih, dan berdaya,” tutup Achmad Siswandi Asdam.

en.title: Synergy for Asta Cita: PT Vale Participates in South Sulawesi’s 356th Anniversary through ‘Sulsel Expo Andalan Hati’
en.subtitle: Aligned with the President’s Asta Cita vision, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening MSMEs—key drivers of the national economy—by actively collaborating with the South Sulawesi Government during the province’s 356th anniversary to boost the real sector.
en.body:
Makassar, October 15, 2025 — In line with the spirit of Asta Cita as envisioned by the President, support for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)—a vital pillar of the national economy—must be continuously strengthened. As part of the 356th Anniversary celebrations of South Sulawesi Province, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PT Vale) actively participated and collaborated with the local government to invigorate the real sector.

As a manifestation of this commitment, PT Vale took part in the UMKM Expo “Andalan Hati”, themed “Sulsel Maju dan Berkarakter 2025” (South Sulawesi: Progressive and Character-Driven 2025), held over five days from October 15 to 19, 2025, at the Mandala Monument, Jenderal Sudirman Street, Makassar.

During the opening ceremony on Wednesday, October 15, 2025, Governor Andi Sudirman Sulaiman expressed his hopes for enhancing the capacity of MSME players. He also acknowledged the contributions of supporting companies, including PT Vale, by presenting a certificate of appreciation for their role in achieving a record-breaking feat: the largest serving of vegetarian dishes and coffee beverages, a highlight of the Expo’s opening festivities.

Empowering Local MSMEs

Endra Kusuma, Head of External Relations at PT Vale Indonesia, emphasized that the company’s presence at the Sulsel Expo reflects its core values of transforming natural resources into sustainable prosperity.

“Today, PT Vale is proud to participate in the UMKM Expo, part of the 356th South Sulawesi Anniversary celebration. We are showcasing a variety of MSME products nurtured through our community development programs, including keripik pangkilang (fish chips), Kopi Matano, banana snacks, red ginger sarabba, teng-teng (traditional peanut snacks), and many more,” he stated.

These products are not merely household creations but the result of ongoing capacity-building efforts by PT Vale in collaboration with communities surrounding its operational areas. For Endra, this participation is a strategic move to expand market access for Vale-supported MSMEs.

“This is our effort to ensure that Vale’s MSME products gain broader recognition—not only in East Luwu but across South Sulawesi,” he added. “We aim to maximize sales and generate tangible economic impact for the community.”

On the first day of the Expo, 150 cups of Kopi Matano were served to visitors, with plans to distribute 50–100 cups daily throughout the event. Coinciding with World Coffee Day and World Vegetarian Day, PT Vale distributed approximately 200 cups of Kopi Matano to attendees.

The coffee originates from farmers in Nuha Village, near Lake Matano, an area adjacent to PT Vale’s nickel mining operations. The beans are processed and served by MSME partners under PT Vale’s guidance.

Government and Private Sector SynergyPT Vale’s support for the 2025 UMKM Expo was warmly received by the South Sulawesi Provincial Government.

“This event is truly remarkable,” said Governor Andi Sudirman after visiting several booths. “The products are impressive. We hope events like this continue and that companies like PT Vale remain committed to supporting them.”

The Governor also highlighted the importance of collaboration between government and private enterprises in strengthening MSME capacity—through training, financial assistance, and product packaging support, especially for MSMEs in rural areas.

Echoing this sentiment, Iqbal Suhaeb, Chair of the South Sulawesi Anniversary Committee, stated that the UMKM Expo is set to become an annual agenda. This year, nearly 100 local MSMEs participated.

“PT Vale is one of the companies supporting this event, and we hope this contribution continues in line with the Governor’s direction,” said Iqbal. “As we know, PT Vale has extensive experience in MSME development—providing capital support, improving business management, marketing, and helping entrepreneurs enhance their competitiveness,” he added.

In addition to showcasing local products and Kopi Matano, PT Vale also demonstrated its commitment to environmental sustainability and healthy living. During the event, which set a record for the largest serving of vegetarian dishes and coffee beverages, PT Vale was honored with an award from the Indonesian World Achievement Institute (LEPRID). The award was presented directly by Paulus Pangka, Founder and Chairman of LEPRID, in recognition of PT Vale’s support in achieving this milestone.

Future Participation in South Sulawesi’s MSME Mall
Looking ahead, PT Vale will also take part in the South Sulawesi Provincial Government’s upcoming MSME Mall initiative—a dedicated space for promoting and marketing local products. “PT Vale will contribute to the MSME Mall by showcasing products from our partner communities,” said Endra Kusuma.

id.title: Sinergi untuk Asta Cita, PT Vale Turut Memeriahkan Hari Jadi Ke-356 Sulsel Melalui 'Sulsel Expo Andalan Hati'
id.subtitle: Sejalan dengan visi Asta Cita Presiden, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk menegaskan komitmennya dalam memperkuat UMKM—penggerak utama ekonomi nasional—dengan berkolaborasi aktif bersama Pemerintah Provinsi Sulawesi Selatan pada perayaan Hari Jadi ke-356 untuk mendorong sektor riil.
id.body:
Makassar, 15 Oktober 2025 — Sejalan dengan semangat Asta Cita Presiden, dukungan untuk para pelaku Usaha Mikro, Kecil dan Menengah (UMKM) sebagai salah satu sektor penopang ekonomi nasional harus terus digalakkan. Melalui rangkaian perayaan Hari Jadi Ke-356 Provinsi Sulawesi Selatan, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PT Vale) turut terlibat dan berkolaborasi dengan pemerintah daerah mengerakkan sektor riil.

Sebagai bagian dari semangat tersebut, PT Vale turut berpartisipasi dalam gelaran bertajuk UMKM Expo 'Andalan Hati' yang mengusung tema “Sulsel Maju dan Berkarakter 2025”, berlangsung selama lima hari, yakni 15 hingga 19 Oktober 2025 di Halaman Monumen Mandala, Jalan Jenderal Sudirman Makassar.

Pada seremonial pembukaan event, Rabu 15 Oktober 2025, Gubernur Andi Sudirman Sulaiman menyampaikan harapannya untuk peningkatan kapasitas para pelaku UMKM.

Tidak lupa, Gubernur juga memanggil para pimpinan perusahaan pendukung, termasuk PT Vale, lalu menyerahkan piagam penghargaan atas kontribusi perusahaan berkelanjutan itu mendukung pencapaian rekor penyajian makanan vegetarian dan minuman kopi terbanyak, salah satu kegiatan yang memeriahkan event pembukaan ekspo .

Endra Kusuma, Head of External Relations PT Vale Indonesia mengungkapkan, kehadiran perusahaan tersebut dalam event Expo Sulsel, tidak terlepas dari nilai-nilai yang dipegang perusahaan, yakni mentransformasi sumber kekayaan alam menjadi kemakmuran yang berkelanjutan.

“Hari ini, PT Vale ikut memeriahkan dan berpartisipasi dalam UMKM Expo yang merupakan rangkaian HUT Sulsel ke-356. Kami membawa berbagai produk UMKM binaan, seperti keripik pangkilang, kopi Matano, camilan pisang, sarabba jahe merah, teng-teng, dan banyak lagi,” ungkapnya.

Produk-produk itu bukan sekadar hasil olahan rumah tangga, tapi buah dari pembinaan berkelanjutan yang dilakukan PT Vale bersama masyarakat di sekitar area operasionalnya. Bagi Endra, keterlibatan ini adalah cara untuk membuka pasar yang lebih luas bagi UMKM binaan Vale.

“Ini upaya kami agar produk binaan Vale dikenal lebih luas, tidak hanya di Luwu Timur, tapi di seluruh Sulawesi Selatan,” lanjutnya. “Kami ingin penjualannya semakin maksimal dan memberikan dampak ekonomi yang nyata bagi masyarakat.”katanya.

Dalam momen yang bertepatan dengan Hari Kopi Sedunia dan Hari Vegetarian Sedunia itu, PT Vale menyajikankan 150 gelas kopi Matano pada hari pertama, dan rencananya pada periode hari berikutnya selama pameran akan diberikan ke pengunjung sebanyak 50-100 gelas kopi.

Kopi Matano berasal dari petani di Desa Nuha, sekitar Danau Matano, wilayah yang berada di dekat operasi tambang nikel PT Vale. Kopi itu kemudian diolah, dan disajikan oleh pelaku UMKM mitra binaan PT Vale Indonesia.

Sinergi Pemerintah dan Dunia Usaha

Dukungan PT Vale dalam UMKM Expo 2025 mendapat apresiasi dari Pemerintah Provinsi Sulsel.

“Kegiatan ini sudah luar biasa,” ungkapnya usai meninjau sejumlah booth. “Saya rasa sudah bagus-bagus produknya. Kita ingin event seperti ini terus berlanjut, dan perusahaan seperti PT Vale terus memberi dukungan,” ungkapnya lagi.

Gubernur Andi Sudirman juga menekankan pentingnya kolaborasi antara pemerintah dan perusahaan swasta dalam memperkuat kapasitas UMKM. Bentuknya bisa berupa pelatihan, bantuan permodalan, hingga pendampingan dalam pengemasan produk. Khususnya bagi pelaku UMKM di daerah.

Senada dengan itu, Ketua Panitia Hari Jadi Sulsel, Iqbal Suhaeb, menjelaskan bahwa event UMKM Expo ini akan menjadi agenda tahunan. Tahun ini, hampir 100 UMKM lokal ikut ambil bagian.

“PT Vale menjadi salah satu perusahaan ikut mendukung event ini, dan kita harap kontribusi ini terus berlanjut sesuai arahan pak Gubernur,” ujar Iqbal. “Seperti kita tahu, PT Vale sudah berpengalaman dalam melakukan pembinaan UMKM, membantu permodalan, membenahi manajemen UMKM, pemasaran dan bisa memfasilitasi pelaku usaha ini untuk punya daya saing tinggi," tuturnya.

Selain menghadirkan produk dan kopi khas Matano, PT Vale juga menunjukkan kepeduliannya terhadap lingkungan dan gaya hidup sehat. Dalam acara yang juga mencatatkan rekor penyajian makanan vegetarian dan minuman kopi terbanyak, PT Vale menjadi salah satu perusahaan yang menerima penghargaan dari Lembaga Prestasi Indonesia Dunia (LEPRID).

Penghargaan tersebut diserahkan langsung oleh Paulus Pangka, Pendiri dan Ketua Umum LEPRID, sebagai bentuk apresiasi atas dukungan PT Vale dalam penyelenggaraan rekor tersebut.

Partisipasi PT Vale untuk Mall UMKM Pemprov Sulsel

Ke depan, PT Vale juga akan berpartisipasi dalam program Pemerintah Provinsi Sulsel yang akan meluncurkan Mall UMKM, sebagai ruang khusus bagi produk lokal untuk dipasarkan lebih luas. "PT Vale akan mengisi mall UMKM dengan produk-produk mitra binaan perusahaan," ungkap Endra Kusuma.

en.title: PT Vale urges nickel producers pivot toward "the right nickel" during LME Week 2025
en.subtitle: As the world’s metals leaders gather for LME Week 2025, PT Vale Indonesia (PTVI) delivers a clear message to the global mining and investment community: the future will not be defined by how much nickel the world produces, but by how responsibly it is produced. At a time when the global nickel market faces a paradox,  oversupply pressures on one side and insatiable demand for clean-energy minerals on the other — PT Vale urges the industry to pivot toward what it calls “the right nickel”: nickel that is low-carbon, ethically mined, and transparently sourced from communities that grow alongside it.
en.body:
London, 14 October, 2025 — As the world’s metals leaders gather for LME Week 2025, PT Vale Indonesia (PTVI) delivers a clear message to the global mining and investment community: the future will not be defined by how much nickel the world produces, but by how responsibly it is produced.

At a time when the global nickel market faces a paradox,  oversupply pressures on one side and insatiable demand for clean-energy minerals on the other — PT Vale urges the industry to pivot toward what it calls “the right nickel”: nickel that is low-carbon, ethically mined, and transparently sourced from communities that grow alongside it. “We cannot power the green revolution with dirty energy,” said Bernardus Irmanto,  President Director & CEO of PT Vale Indonesia. “The world doesn’t need just more nickel. It needs the right nickel, one produced with integrity, decarbonized at its source, and grounded in respect for people and the planet.”

Across the metals sector, a new reality is taking shape. The climate crisis is accelerating. Financing is shifting toward ESG-compliant operations. Communities are demanding accountability. Yet, global demand for critical minerals — particularly nickel for electric vehicle batteries and renewable storage — continues to rise.

For PT Vale, this convergence represents not a burden but a call to leadership. For over five decades, the company has operated in Indonesia’s rich nickel belt, balancing industrial progress with environmental care. Now, as the conversation at LME Week turns to the role of metals in achieving net-zero, PTVI steps forward with a vision that blends responsibility with opportunity. “Our goal is not only to supply the world with nickel, but to redefine what responsible supply looks like,” Anto added. “That means traceable operations, transparent governance, and tangible community partnerships that endure beyond mine life.”

 
One if this deliberate evolution comes from PT Vale’s story. In 2017, long before “green nickel” entered global vocabulary, the company pledged to cut one-third of its carbon intensity by 2030. At the time, the solutions did not yet exist, but the conviction did.

That conviction has since sparked a wave of innovation: the installation of electric boilers to replace fossil-fuel combustion, waste-heat recovery systems that convert energy losses into power, and ore-dewatering initiatives that optimize water use while improving efficiency. Each investment, while technical in nature, serves a singular purpose — proving that decarbonization and profitability can coexist.

In parallel, PT Vale is reinforcing governance through rigorous global standards. Its flagship operation in Sorowako is now undergoing independent verification under the Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance (IRMA) — among the most stringent mining standards in the world. Audits for its upcoming projects in Bahodopi and Pomalaa will follow.

These actions, combined with over fifty years of community partnerships and recognized performance — including multiple Green PROPER awards and Gold from Indonesia’s Ministry of Environment and a Sustainalytics ESG Risk Rating of 27.5 — position PT Vale among the world’s most trusted nickel producers.

This week in London, as global conversations at LME Week revolve around market volatility, geopolitical realignment, and the decarbonization of metals, PT Vale offers a simple yet powerful idea: trust is the new currency of mining.

In an era when every supply chain is scrutinized, when every tonne of ore carries a carbon footprint, and when communities demand participation, the right nickel is more than a product, it is a promise.

“We believe sustainability is not a cost,” said Anto, “It is who we are — our identity, our advantage, and our contribution to a future where industry and nature can coexist. Our legacy will not be measured by how much we produce, but by the impact we leave behind.”

As the global metals market recalibrates, PT Vale invites partners, investors, and policymakers to collaborate in shaping a resilient and ethical nickel industry, one that powers not only batteries, but hope, resilience, and progress.

id.title: PT Vale Serukan Produsen Nikel Beralih ke “Nikel yang Tepat” dalam LME Week 2025
id.subtitle: Dalam perhelatan LME Week 2025 yang mempertemukan para pemimpin industri logam dunia, PT Vale Indonesia (PTVI) menyampaikan pesan tegas kepada komunitas pertambangan dan investor global: masa depan industri nikel tidak ditentukan oleh seberapa banyak nikel yang diproduksi, melainkan oleh bagaimana nikel tersebut diproduksi secara bertanggung jawab. Di tengah paradoks pasar nikel global — tekanan kelebihan pasokan di satu sisi dan permintaan tinggi terhadap mineral energi bersih di sisi lain — PT Vale mengajak industri untuk beralih ke apa yang disebut sebagai “nikel yang tepat” (the right nickel): yakni nikel rendah karbon, ditambang secara etis, dan bersumber secara transparan dari komunitas yang turut berkembang bersama operasionalnya.
id.body:
London, 14 Oktober 2025 — Dalam perhelatan LME Week 2025 yang mempertemukan para pemimpin industri logam dunia, PT Vale Indonesia (PTVI) menyampaikan pesan tegas kepada komunitas pertambangan dan investor global: masa depan industri nikel tidak ditentukan oleh seberapa banyak nikel yang diproduksi, melainkan oleh bagaimana nikel tersebut diproduksi secara bertanggung jawab.

Di tengah paradoks pasar nikel global — tekanan kelebihan pasokan di satu sisi dan permintaan tinggi terhadap mineral energi bersih di sisi lain — PT Vale mengajak industri untuk beralih ke apa yang disebut sebagai “nikel yang tepat” (the right nickel): yakni nikel rendah karbon, ditambang secara etis, dan bersumber secara transparan dari komunitas yang turut berkembang bersama operasionalnya.

“Kita tidak bisa mendukung revolusi hijau dengan energi yang kotor,” ujar Bernardus Irmanto, Presiden Direktur & CEO PT Vale Indonesia. “Dunia tidak hanya membutuhkan lebih banyak nikel. Dunia membutuhkan nikel yang tepat — yang diproduksi dengan integritas, didekarbonisasi sejak dari sumbernya, dan berlandaskan pada penghormatan terhadap manusia dan lingkungan.”

Di seluruh sektor logam, realitas baru tengah terbentuk. Krisis iklim semakin mendesak. Pendanaan global mulai beralih ke operasi yang sesuai prinsip ESG. Komunitas menuntut akuntabilitas. Namun, permintaan global terhadap mineral kritis — khususnya nikel untuk baterai kendaraan listrik dan penyimpanan energi terbarukan — terus meningkat.

Bagi PT Vale, konvergensi ini bukanlah beban, melainkan panggilan untuk memimpin. Selama lebih dari lima dekade, perusahaan telah beroperasi di kawasan nikel Indonesia dengan menyeimbangkan kemajuan industri dan kepedulian lingkungan. Kini, saat diskusi di LME Week berfokus pada peran logam dalam mencapai target net-zero, PTVI hadir dengan visi yang memadukan tanggung jawab dan peluang.

“Tujuan kami bukan sekadar memasok nikel ke dunia, tetapi mendefinisikan ulang seperti apa pasokan yang bertanggung jawab,” tambah Anto. “Itu berarti operasi yang dapat ditelusuri, tata kelola yang transparan, dan kemitraan komunitas yang berkelanjutan bahkan setelah tambang berhenti beroperasi.”

 

Evolusi ini bukan hal baru bagi PT Vale. Pada 2017, jauh sebelum istilah “green nickel” populer secara global, perusahaan telah berkomitmen mengurangi sepertiga intensitas karbonnya pada 2030. Saat itu, solusi teknisnya belum tersedia, namun keyakinan sudah ada.

Keyakinan tersebut kini melahirkan berbagai inovasi: pemasangan boiler listrik untuk menggantikan pembakaran bahan bakar fosil, sistem pemulihan panas buangan untuk menghasilkan energi, serta inisiatif dewatering bijih yang mengoptimalkan penggunaan air sekaligus meningkatkan efisiensi. Setiap investasi ini, meski bersifat teknis, memiliki satu tujuan utama — membuktikan bahwa dekarbonisasi dan profitabilitas dapat berjalan beriringan.

Secara paralel, PT Vale memperkuat tata kelola melalui standar global yang ketat. Operasi utama di Sorowako kini tengah menjalani verifikasi independen di bawah Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance (IRMA) — salah satu standar pertambangan paling ketat di dunia. Audit untuk proyek Bahodopi dan Pomalaa akan menyusul.

Langkah-langkah ini, ditambah dengan lebih dari lima dekade kemitraan komunitas dan rekam jejak kinerja yang diakui — termasuk berbagai penghargaan PROPER Hijau dan Emas dari Kementerian Lingkungan Hidup serta ESG Risk Rating 27,5 dari Sustainalytics — menempatkan PT Vale sebagai salah satu produsen nikel paling tepercaya di dunia.

Minggu ini di London, saat diskusi global di LME Week berkisar pada volatilitas pasar, pergeseran geopolitik, dan dekarbonisasi logam, PT Vale menawarkan satu gagasan sederhana namun kuat: kepercayaan adalah mata uang baru dalam industri pertambangan.
Di era ketika setiap rantai pasok diawasi, setiap ton bijih membawa jejak karbon, dan komunitas menuntut keterlibatan, “the right nickel” bukan sekadar produk — melainkan janji. “Kami percaya bahwa keberlanjutan bukanlah biaya,” tutup Anto. “Keberlanjutan adalah jati diri kami — keunggulan kami, dan kontribusi kami untuk masa depan di mana industri dan alam dapat hidup berdampingan. Warisan kami tidak akan diukur dari seberapa banyak kami memproduksi, tetapi dari dampak yang kami tinggalkan.”

Saat pasar logam global melakukan rekalibrasi, PT Vale mengundang mitra, investor, dan pembuat kebijakan untuk bersama-sama membentuk industri nikel yang tangguh dan etis — industri yang tidak hanya menjadi penggerak baterai, tetapi juga harapan, ketahanan, dan kemajuan.

en.title: Maravilhas III Dam: September Updates
en.subtitle: The Maravilhas III Dam, located in Nova Lima, Minas Gerais, maintained an adequate conservation status throughout September 2025.
en.body:
The Maravilhas III Dam, located in Nova Lima, Minas Gerais, maintained an adequate conservation status throughout September 2025.

To monitor the geotechnical performance of the structure, we rely on the support of an external company, the Registered Engineer (RE). The Geotechnical Performance Assessment Report prepared by the RE for the month of September indicates that, based on data obtained through monitoring and visual inspections, the dam is performing within normal parameters. Additionally, the geotechnical instruments are operating within expected ranges, and the safety factors obtained from stability analyses continue to meet the minimum requirements established by current legislation.

Construction works for the second stage of the dam’s embankment are ongoing, including the placement of compacted fill downstream of the existing structure and continued excavation of the abutments for terrain cleaning and slope adjustment. The downstream area is in the final phase of slope regularization and flow direction, and the Rockfill Dike is nearing its final design configuration. Furthermore, maintenance activities were carried out on the structure, such as vegetation clearing, cleaning, and painting of surface drainage devices.

In accordance with the submission cycle to the National Mining Agency, the Stability Condition Declaration (DCE) for Maravilhas III was updated in September, remaining positive, with no alert or emergency level associated with the structure. The dam continues to be monitored 24/7 by the Geotechnical Monitoring Center (CMG).

en.title: Indonesia at the Epicenter of Critical Minerals: Forging the Future of Sustainable Energy
en.subtitle: Indonesia took center stage at the Indonesia International Sustainability Forum (IISF) with a landmark dialogue highlighting the nation’s defining role in the global energy transition. The 90-minute session, hosted by PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PT Vale) and titled “Indonesia at the Epicenter of Critical Minerals: Nickel, Copper, and the Global Energy Transition,” convened leading voices from government, industry, and sustainability institutions.
en.body:
Jakarta, 10 October 2025 — Indonesia took center stage at the Indonesia International Sustainability Forum (IISF) with a landmark dialogue highlighting the nation’s defining role in the global energy transition.

The 90-minute session, hosted by PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PT Vale) and titled “Indonesia at the Epicenter of Critical Minerals: Nickel, Copper, and the Global Energy Transition,” convened leading voices from government, industry, and sustainability institutions. Together, they explored how Indonesia can balance its vast resource potential with environmental stewardship, social inclusion, and long-term economic resilience.

Moderated by Rajat Agarwal, Partner at McKinsey & Company, the session featured Bernardus Irmanto (President Director & CEO, PT Vale Indonesia), Dr. Ing. Tri Winarno (Director General of Mineral and Coal, Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources), David Wei (General Manager, Huayou Indonesia), and Rebecca Burton (Deputy Director, Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance – IRMA).

Global demand for nickel and copper; two essential minerals for electric vehicles, renewable energy, and electrification is expected to double or triple by 2040. Indonesia, home to the world’s largest nickel reserves and fast-growing copper operations, stands at the center of this transformation. “Critical minerals are the foundation of the global energy transition, and Indonesia sits at its epicenter,” said Bernardus Irmanto, CEO of PT Vale Indonesia. “Our mission is not only to meet global demand but to meet it responsibly, ensuring that sustainability, transparency, and community empowerment define how Indonesia contributes to the world’s net-zero future.”

Representing the government’s strategic direction, Dr. Ing. Tri Winarno, Director General of Mineral and Coal, Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (KESDM), emphasized the importance of integrating sustainability into Indonesia’s downstream and decarbonization strategy. “Indonesia’s commitment to responsible mineral development is clear, we must pursue industrial growth without compromising environmental balance,” Dr. Winarno stated. “Through innovation, collaboration, and adherence to international standards, Indonesia will continue to strengthen its leadership in the global energy transition while delivering value to its people.”

From the perspective of the global mining industry, David Wei, General Manager of Huayou Indonesia, underscored the significance of building long-term, responsible partnerships that prioritize both innovation and sustainability.“Sustainability is no longer optional , it defines global credibility,” said Wei.“Our collaboration with PT Vale shows how industry partnerships can drive responsible sourcing, carbon reduction, and shared prosperity. The future of critical minerals depends on how we grow together, with integrity and impact.”

Providing the global ESG lens, Rebecca Burton, Deputy Director of the Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance (IRMA), shared that international standards can act as a bridge between Indonesia’s industrial leadership and the expectations of global markets. “Investors and manufacturers worldwide increasingly demand verified proof of responsible practices,” Burton said. “IRMA serves as that bridge, connecting Indonesia’s mining sector to global trust by ensuring transparency, independent assurance, and respect for both people and nature. This alignment can set a new global benchmark for emerging economies.”

The session concluded with a shared commitment: that Indonesia’s mineral leadership must go beyond production metrics, it must represent a values-driven approach to growth. “We believe Indonesia’s true potential lies in leading not only by scale, but by standards,” Bernardus concluded. “By embedding sustainability into the core of our operations, we are commited to ensure that every ton of nickel mined in Indonesia contributes to the world’s cleaner, fairer, and more sustainable future.”

id.title: Indonesia di Pusat Mineral Kritis: Menempa Masa Depan Energi Berkelanjutan
id.subtitle: Indonesia menjadi sorotan utama dalam ajang Indonesia International Sustainability Forum (IISF) melalui sesi dialog strategis yang menegaskan peran penting bangsa ini dalam transisi energi global. Sesi berdurasi 90 menit yang diselenggarakan oleh PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PT Vale) dengan tajuk “Indonesia at the Epicenter of Critical Minerals: Nickel, Copper, and the Global Energy Transition” ini menghadirkan para pemimpin dari kalangan pemerintah, industri, dan lembaga keberlanjutan.
id.body:
Jakarta, 10 Oktober 2025 — Indonesia menjadi sorotan utama dalam ajang Indonesia International Sustainability Forum (IISF) melalui sesi dialog strategis yang menegaskan peran penting bangsa ini dalam transisi energi global.

Sesi berdurasi 90 menit yang diselenggarakan oleh PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PT Vale) dengan tajuk “Indonesia at the Epicenter of Critical Minerals: Nickel, Copper, and the Global Energy Transition” ini menghadirkan para pemimpin dari kalangan pemerintah, industri, dan lembaga keberlanjutan. Bersama-sama, mereka membahas bagaimana Indonesia dapat menyeimbangkan potensi sumber daya alamnya yang besar dengan tanggung jawab lingkungan, inklusi sosial, serta ketahanan ekonomi jangka panjang.

Sesi ini dimoderatori oleh Rajat Agarwal, Partner di McKinsey & Company, dan menampilkan pembicara Bernardus Irmanto (President Director & CEO PT Vale Indonesia), Dr. Ing. Tri Winarno (Direktur Jenderal Mineral dan Batubara, Kementerian Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral), David Wei (General Manager, Huayou Indonesia), serta Rebecca Burton (Deputy Director, Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance – IRMA).

Permintaan global terhadap nikel dan tembaga—dua mineral penting bagi kendaraan listrik, energi terbarukan, dan elektrifikasi—diproyeksikan meningkat dua hingga tiga kali lipat pada tahun 2040. Indonesia, yang memiliki cadangan nikel terbesar di dunia dan tengah mengembangkan sektor tembaganya dengan pesat, berada di pusat transformasi ini. “Mineral kritis merupakan fondasi dari transisi energi global, dan Indonesia berada tepat di episentrumnya,” ujar Bernardus Irmanto, CEO PT Vale Indonesia. “Misi kami bukan sekadar memenuhi permintaan dunia, tetapi memenuhinya secara bertanggung jawab—dengan menjadikan keberlanjutan, transparansi, dan pemberdayaan masyarakat sebagai landasan kontribusi Indonesia menuju masa depan net-zero dunia.”

Mewakili arah strategis pemerintah, Dr. Ing. Tri Winarno, Direktur Jenderal Mineral dan Batubara Kementerian ESDM, menekankan pentingnya integrasi aspek keberlanjutan dalam strategi hilirisasi dan dekarbonisasi nasional. “Komitmen Indonesia terhadap pengelolaan mineral yang bertanggung jawab sangat jelas. Kita harus mengejar pertumbuhan industri tanpa mengorbankan keseimbangan lingkungan,” tegas Dr. Winarno. “Melalui inovasi, kolaborasi, dan penerapan standar internasional, Indonesia akan terus memperkuat kepemimpinannya dalam transisi energi global sekaligus memberikan manfaat nyata bagi rakyatnya.”

Dari perspektif industri pertambangan global, David Wei, General Manager Huayou Indonesia, menyoroti pentingnya membangun kemitraan jangka panjang yang bertanggung jawab dan menyeimbangkan inovasi dengan keberlanjutan. “Keberlanjutan kini bukan lagi pilihan, melainkan penentu kredibilitas global,” kata Wei. “Kolaborasi kami dengan PT Vale menunjukkan bagaimana kemitraan industri dapat mendorong praktik penambangan yang bertanggung jawab, pengurangan karbon, serta kesejahteraan bersama. Masa depan mineral kritis akan bergantung pada kemampuan kita untuk tumbuh bersama dengan integritas dan dampak positif.”

Dari perspektif tata kelola global, Rebecca Burton, Deputy Director IRMA, menjelaskan bahwa standar internasional dapat menjadi jembatan antara kepemimpinan industri Indonesia dan ekspektasi pasar global. “Investor dan produsen di seluruh dunia kini semakin menuntut bukti nyata praktik yang bertanggung jawab,” ujar Burton. “IRMA hadir sebagai jembatan yang menghubungkan sektor pertambangan Indonesia dengan kepercayaan global melalui transparansi, verifikasi independen, dan penghormatan terhadap manusia serta alam. Penyelarasan ini dapat menjadi tolok ukur baru bagi negara-negara berkembang lainnya.”

Sesi ini ditutup dengan komitmen bersama bahwa kepemimpinan Indonesia dalam mineral kritis harus melampaui ukuran produksi semata—namun mencerminkan pertumbuhan yang berlandaskan nilai. “Kami percaya potensi sejati Indonesia tidak hanya diukur dari skala produksi, tetapi dari standar yang kami junjung,” pungkas Bernardus. “Dengan menanamkan keberlanjutan ke dalam inti operasi kami, kami berkomitmen memastikan setiap ton nikel yang ditambang di Indonesia berkontribusi bagi masa depan yang lebih bersih, adil, dan berkelanjutan bagi dunia.”

en.title: Brazilian Mining Sector Presents Pathways to Reduce Carbon Emissions by Up to 90% by 2050
en.subtitle: Study by the Essential Minerals Coalition, led by CEBDS, Vale, and IBRAM, presented to the President of COP30
en.body:
A study conducted by the Essential Minerals Coalition—an initiative led by the Brazilian Business Council for Sustainable Development (CEBDS), Vale, and the Brazilian Mining Institute (IBRAM)—was presented on Thursday, October 9, to Ambassador André Corrêa do Lago, President of COP30. The study outlines potential pathways for the mining sector to reduce its own carbon emissions by up to 90% and contribute to Brazil’s overall emissions reduction targets by 2050. It also highlights the sector’s potential to lower global emissions in the steel value chain and support the global electrification process.

The Coalition was formed in response to an invitation from the COP30 Presidency, which encouraged six key sectors of the Brazilian economy—agriculture, energy, forestry, mining, livestock, and transportation—to mobilize and propose decarbonization strategies to be presented at the COP30 event in Belém this November.

 

The study emphasizes that the global energy transition is intrinsically linked to mining, and that Brazil is strategically positioned in this context due to its vast geological diversity, a well-developed mining sector, and a predominantly renewable energy matrix, among other factors. In addition to identifying the sector’s potential contributions to energy transition and economic decarbonization, the report outlines five prerequisites necessary to unlock this potential in the coming years.

“The coalitions embody the collaborative spirit that COP30 seeks to inspire: companies, government, and civil society working together in a pre-competitive and science-aligned manner to build sectoral consensus and actionable solutions. This initiative marks the beginning of a journey that goes beyond paper—transforming consensus into implementation for a low-carbon economy. In this movement, the Essential Minerals Coalition plays a strategic role by proposing concrete pathways to decarbonize its value chain and support the global energy transition,” said Marina Grossi, President of CEBDS.

“Private sector engagement is essential for advancing the climate agenda in Brazil. For Vale, which places decarbonization at the core of its business strategy, it is an honor to co-lead this initiative—especially at a time when energy transition minerals are gaining geopolitical relevance. Brazil is at the center of this discussion, with significant potential to produce these minerals and as one of the world’s leading producers of high-quality iron ore, which is critical for decarbonizing the steel industry,” said Gustavo Pimenta, President of Vale.

“The report demonstrates that mining is a key pillar in solving the climate crisis,” stated Raul Jungmann, President of IBRAM. “Brazil holds a unique competitive advantage, with geological diversity and a clean energy matrix. The study shows we are ready to supply the minerals the world needs to build a low-carbon economy—but we cannot do it alone.”

 

Levers for emissions reduction

The Coalition analyzed three scopes of mining’s contribution to global decarbonization and the energy transition. The first scope, focused on reducing emissions from mining operations themselves, identified a potential reduction of up to 80% in sector emissions, along with the neutralization of approximately 14% of residual emissions—resulting in a total reduction of around 90% by 2050. Five key levers were defined to achieve this scenario: energy efficiency; use of biofuels; expansion of electricity from renewable sources; electrification of fleets and equipment; and rehabilitation of degraded areas to offset residual emissions.

A second scope, dedicated to mining’s contribution to reducing emissions in the global iron ore value chain, indicated that reductions could reach 110 MtCO₂e by 2050—equivalent to eight times the annual emissions of the Brazilian mining sector in 2022. This would be achieved through the production of low-carbon steel inputs, such as pellets and briquettes for direct reduction routes. Additional reductions may be possible in activities such as pelletizing, rail transport, and international shipping, depending on economic instruments and enabling conditions outlined in the study.

Regarding energy transition minerals—such as copper, nickel, bauxite, lithium, rare earths, among others—the Coalition estimates that Brazil’s mining sector could double production by 2050, potentially reducing the country’s total emissions by up to 300 MtCO₂e annually by 2050. This figure is equivalent to the combined emissions of the states of São Paulo and Minas Gerais in 2023.

This scenario considers the global increase in electric vehicle production by up to 38 million additional units by 2050, the expansion of installed wind energy capacity by up to 830 GW, solar energy by up to 610 GW, and the growth of power grids and energy storage systems worldwide.

The study also emphasizes that unlocking Brazil’s mining potential depends on the creation of a favorable environment, structured around five key prerequisites: improvements in the regulatory and economic landscape, including the implementation of carbon pricing; increased access to mature and economically viable technologies; sufficiently robust logistics, energy, and storage infrastructure; consolidated green financial instruments and sustainable taxonomies; and a “green premium”—an additional payment for products with a lower carbon footprint—alongside incentives throughout the value chain to promote practices such as circularity.

 

About the Essential Minerals Coalition

The Essential Minerals Coalition was established as part of the “Global Taskforce” convened by the COP30 Presidency. Bringing together companies, associations, experts, and government representatives, the Coalition consolidated a shared vision for the future—aligning the Brazilian mining sector’s contributions with national and international commitments to decarbonization and energy transition. This collective effort was built through workshops, interviews, and sectoral analyses, culminating in a report that synthesizes the sector’s potential for positive impact and the systemic enablers required to realize it.

 

About CEBDS

The Brazilian Business Council for Sustainable Development (CEBDS) is a non-profit civil association that has been promoting sustainable development in Brazil since 1997. It does so by engaging with governments and civil society, and by disseminating the most current concepts and practices related to sustainability. As the voice of the business sector, CEBDS brings together more than 110 of the country’s largest business groups and serves as the Brazilian representative of the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD), which operates in 36 countries and includes 200 member companies worldwide.

 

About Vale 

Vale is a global mining company that exists to improve lives and transform the future together. One of the world’s largest producers of iron ore and nickel, and a significant producer of copper, Vale is headquartered in Brazil and operates globally. Its operations include integrated logistics systems, comprising approximately 2,000 kilometers of railways, maritime terminals, and 20 ports across the world.

Vale aspires to be recognized by society as a benchmark in safety, the most reliable and efficient operator, a talent-driven organization, a leader in sustainable mining, and a reference in value creation and sharing.

 

About IBRAM 

The Brazilian Mining Institute (IBRAM) is a private, non-profit organization with over 300 member companies, responsible for 85% of Brazil’s mineral production. IBRAM represents ethical, transparent, and inclusive mining, committed to best practices in ESG. For decades, it has promoted socioeconomic development and quality of life. Its initiatives aim to build a more productive and sustainable future for the mining sector.
IBRAM leads the transition to responsible and safe mining, strengthening relationships among mining companies, government, society, and suppliers. It fosters innovation, disseminates knowledge, and facilitates business opportunities. The institute promotes best practices and connects stakeholders across the sector. Open to dialogue with public and private organizations, IBRAM operates with competence, active listening, and strong engagement.
